metadata.title: This Week: What Shipped
metadata.register: Professional, polite, simple -- a real progress update, not overhyped, per the user's explicit tone request.
metadata.note: A CLI-explainer weekly recap -- a separate week's log from this user's earlier weekly-recap builds (weekly-recap, weekly-recap-catbot, weekly-recap-suffolk). Built around a real weekly_recap_v1.py, revised into weekly_recap_v2.py to tag each item by category and print a shipped-count -- both scripts real, both actually run. Unlike the prior weekly-recap builds, this week has no upcoming/next-week item (the user's kickoff lists three items, all already done: article published, four videos produced, one meeting attended) -- so the v1->v2 revision is NOT a DONE/NEXT split; it's a flat-list-to-tagged-and-counted revision, a genuinely different but equally real code change. Self-intro ('Hi, I'm Agrima') folds into B00's own narration per this skill's own convention (not split into a dedicated beat -- that's the ai-explainer-chassis convention used on this user's other builds, a different skill). No dedicated footage exists for this topic per the user's own materials note -- every visual is a generated Manim graphic: a mock Substack article header, a four-video 2x2 grid, and a calendar/meeting icon.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW -- ask shown answered; self-intro folded into this beat's own narration per cli-explainer's convention
beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Agrima. Every week I ask Claude to help me build an honest log of what actually got done -- no highlight reel, just the real list.

props.command:
claude "help me build a real log of what I actually
  did this week"

beats.role_note: a flat list doesn't tell you what kind of week it was, or how much shipped -- sets up the v1->v2 revision
beats.narration_text: This isn't a highlight reel. It's a flat log of what actually happened -- but a flat list doesn't tell you what's writing, what's video, and what's meetings, or just how much got shipped.
So I asked Claude directly: write me a script that logs this week -- the article, the videos, the meeting.

props.command:
claude "write weekly_recap_v1.py -- log this week:
  the article, the videos, the meeting"

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat -- the ACTUAL generated code; weekly_recap_v1.py was really run -- THE ACTUAL-CODE LAW
beats.narration_text: Here's what it wrote -- a flat list, three entries, no ranking, no spin. Just what got published, what got produced, and what got attended.

props.title: weekly_recap_v1.py
props.code:
WEEK = [
    {"item": "Published \"The AI That Never Forgets\" on Substack",
     "where": "substack.com"},
    {"item": "Produced four Brutalist videos (16:9 + 9:16 each)",
     "where": "brutalist.art"},
    {"item": "Attended this week's team meeting",
     "where": "weekly sync"},
]

def log():
    for entry in WEEK:
        print(f"- {entry['item']}  ({entry['where']})")

beats.role_note: three same-weight cards -- article / four videos / meeting -- no labels, no count yet
beats.narration_text: One article, published on Substack. Four videos, produced end to end. One meeting, attended. Three cards, no labels, no count yet -- just the raw list, exactly as the script printed it.
beats.visual_intent: three same-weight cards: mock article header, four-video grid, meeting/calendar icon

beats.role_note: the change: revise v1 -> v2, tag by category, print a shipped-count
beats.narration_text: So the next ask was simple: tag each item by category, and print how many things actually shipped this week.

props.command:
claude "update weekly_recap_v1.py -> weekly_recap_v2.py:
  -> tag each item by category, print a shipped-count"

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat -- the ACTUAL revised code; weekly_recap_v2.py was really run -- THE ACTUAL-CODE LAW
beats.narration_text: Here's the update -- same three entries, but each one tagged, and a count printed at the top.

props.title: weekly_recap_v2.py

beats.role_note: same three cards, now tagged by category with a shipped-count header
beats.narration_text: Writing. Video. Meetings. Three different categories, three different kinds of work this week -- and this time, the count comes with the list: three things, shipped.
beats.visual_intent: same three cards as B04, now with category tag chips and a 'This week: 3 things shipped' header

beats.role_note: closing typographic beat -- what actually shipped, not everything considered
beats.narration_text: Not everything I thought about this week. Not everything I planned to get to. Just what actually shipped -- that's the only log worth keeping, and the only one worth showing.
